newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB changes transaction account products.
newsitem.headline: NAB changes transaction account products.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Friday it would introduce a new transaction account and alter the fee structure of two transaction accounts following a six month review of its transaction products.
NAB said the new transactiuon account would be called National Flexidirect and would meet the growing need for fee-free electronic transactions.
The bank said it would increase the charges on its National FlexiAccounts and National Passbook accounts and also introduce an account keeping fee on these accounts.
NAB said it would reward customer loyalty by exempting fees for customers who had mortgages, cash management accounts and a variety of other accounts.
The bank said it would also give fee concessions for customers with disabilities and would not change the fee structure of its retirement accounts.
"The majority of National's existing customers will not pay an account keeping or transaction banking fee," the bank said in a statement.
NAB said in the past transaction account fees had not reflected the true cost of providing that service.

"While some people may believe that fees of any type are unfair, the reality is that the majority of bank customers have been subsidising a smaller group," NAB'schief general manager, Frank Cicutto said.
Cicutto said the bank's new approach was to reward those customers who had a strong relationship while at the same time meet the needs of those that just wanted a simple transaction account.
NAB said the changes would take effect from October 1 and all account holders would be notified by mail in August.
